ctx.x: Mayor Morrison. It could have been Morrison, I think. It was Morrison. Mayor Morrison. And so they, the laws made no trouble for Mr. Hayes. He made sure that they wouldn't make any trouble because he kept a very unique place, very likable place. People seemed to enjoy themselves when they came here. You had to come in there well, well-groomed, and your mannerism had to be at the highest level in order to get service. He made sure that everything was above board.
Was that, would you say, that that was true of most establishments, black establishments in the city?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: When Mayor Morrison became, became mayor for the city of New Orleans, things were beginning to change.

But then again, you have to thank people like, like, Jack Moore and a few other people, Champ Clark. Then you had people like, Wendy, New Orleans Recreation Department, Jeff was put together. Jeff, Jeff, Jeff, Morris, I think, Jeff was the first black to get involved. Morris, Jeff was a graduate of Zive University and also Chicago University. And he opened many doors for young kids to come out. And they…
